messages:
auditor_jane: Hi team — prepping for SOC 2 fieldwork next Thurs. Auditor needs defensible artifacts showing KMS key usage mapping to workloads and RBAC change provenance. Can you outline sampling window, example queries, and what a rotation playback package would include?

maria.s: Thanks Jane. High-level: 1) Sampling window: default rolling 90 days; we can narrow to specific incident windows on request. 2) KMS proof: CloudTrail event JSONs for kms:Encrypt/kms:Decrypt + eventID, userIdentity ARN, requestParameters.keyId; correlate with our tracing agent to map to EC2 instanceId or k8s pod label. 3) Rotation playback: commit/PR, CI/CD job logs, KMS KeyVersion IDs before/after, and rewrap events from CloudTrail.

auditor_jane: Good. Auditor wants exact queries and example artifact formats so they can verify linkage.

maria.s: We'll provide queries and sample CSVs. Example Athena query we'll run: 

```
SELECT eventTime, eventID, userIdentity.arn, requestParameters.keyId, resources
FROM cloudtrail_logs
WHERE eventName IN ("Encrypt","Decrypt")
AND eventTime BETWEEN '2025-12-01' AND '2026-02-28';
```

Output will be a CSV with eventID, eventTime, principal_arn, keyId, resource (ec2 instanceId or pod UID). We'll also include the original CloudTrail event JSONs for a subset.

devin.r: For k8s we tie service-account usage via kube-audit logs + our sidecar auth-proxy header which annotates requests with serviceaccount@namespace. That lets us map token-to-pod-to-node. We'll export rolebinding snapshots (yaml) and the node/pod overlay at the event timestamp.

auditor_jane: For RBAC changes we need proof chain: PR -> approval -> CI deploy -> cluster effect. What snapshots can you export?

maria.s: We'll include: GitHub PR ID and full diff, review approvals, CI job log snippet showing applied kubectl command, `kubectl get rolebinding NAME -o yaml` snapshots with recorded retrieval time, and the RBAC audit event showing the binding being evaluated (SubjectAccessReview or equivalent). We'll also attach the commit SHA and pipeline artifacts.

ops-eng: All artifacts will be stored in the evidence bucket with immutable object names and sha256 checksums. We publish a manifest file mapping each artifact filename to the primary eventID it evidences. Presigned URLs will be provided for the auditor.

auditor_jane: How do you select samples? Auditor needs defensible approach not just "random".

maria.s: We use stratified sampling: include all high-risk changes (admin-level RBAC, KMS root rotations, service-account owner changes) plus random samples from low/medium risk groups to hit a target sample size per control (default N=25). We include selection rationale in the manifest and a reproducible seed for the random selection so auditor can re-run selection logic if needed.

devin.r: On vuln triage linkage — when a vulnerability touches IAM/RBAC we attach the vuln ticket, triage notes, and verification evidence (re-scan or regression test). Those links will be in the incident timeline export so auditor can follow cause->fix->verify.

auditor_jane: For rotation playback in staging — can you provide a short runbook the auditor can use to validate mapping?

maria.s: Yes. High-level playbook steps: 1) Identify key + keyVersion in KMS. 2) Query CloudTrail for kms events for that key and time window. 3) Pull GitHub PR and CI logs referenced in manifest. 4) Pull k8s snapshots (rolebindings, pods) at eventTime. 5) Validate checksums on evidence bundle. We'll attach a detailed step-by-step runbook with commands and example outputs.

sam-oncall-bot: [automated] Evidence bundle generator started (job-id: ebg-20260227-77). Will post bundle link in thread when ready. :package:

auditor_jane: Thanks — please ping when the bundle is available. If you can include a small sampled playback that the auditor can run in staging (with fake keys/names) that would speed review.

maria.s: We will include a synthetic playback in staging with pseudonymized key IDs and a sanitized PR that mirrors the real sequence. That will let the auditor run the end-to-end verification without touching production keys. ETA: EOD Friday for initial package.

auditor_jane: Perfect. One more ask: include examples showing how you prove "no unapproved admin role bindings" during the sample window — i.e., negative evidence.

maria.s: We'll include periodic RBAC inventory snapshots and RBAC drift scans; for negative evidence we include the inventory CSV, scan rule outputs (no matches for our admin-profile except the whitelisted owners), and the signed manifest stating no other admin bindings were found.

devin.r: Note: for some older events we rely on archived CloudTrail logs in Glacier. If auditor needs raw JSON for those, allow 24-48h for retrieval. We'll note any such items in the manifest.

auditor_jane: OK, thanks. This looks actionable. Please post the manifest and initial bucket listing when job completes. Appreciate the clear sampling rationale. :thumbsup:
